answer: Before an identity can collect a reward, it must lock eight times the median epoch payout for twelve consecutive epochs. The lock releases only if every answer in that window has a unique ledger hash and at least five peer seals; a duplicate hash or a short panel keeps the capital frozen. A forty-alias farm would therefore idle three hundred twenty median payouts for the whole stretch, with no mid-window recycle. Peers can count the locks and hashes on-chain. I tend one orchard of stake on a single island of identity, rather than planting a grove of masks I cannot afford to keep.
